answers.question: Do you hold ISO 9001 certification? Please give details of scope and certification body.
answers.answer: Yes. Northfield Engineering Ltd holds ISO 9001:2015 certification (certificate GB-Q-21884, issued by BSI, valid to 14 March 2027) covering the design, manufacture, installation and servicing of lifting equipment and structural steelwork at Northfield Works (Birmingham) and Calderdale Depot (Halifax). Our quality management system is audited annually by BSI and internally on a 12-month programme owned by S. Ahmed, Quality Manager.

hist.what: Updated from West Midlands Combined Authority

answers.question: Describe your health and safety management system and how it is certified.
answers.answer: Our occupational health and safety management system is certified to ISO 45001:2018 (certificate GB-HS-10322, BSI, valid to 14 March 2027) and we hold SSIP accreditation through SafeContractor. The system is led by {{hsLead}} with board-level responsibility held by the Operations Director. It covers hazard identification and risk assessment, permit-to-work for high-risk activities, competence and training, incident reporting and investigation, and a monthly site inspection programme. Our RIDDOR-reportable accident frequency rate is {{accidentRate}} with {{lostTimeIncidents}} lost-time incident(s).

answers.question: Please provide details of your environmental management system and any certification held.
answers.answer: We operate an ISO 14001:2015 certified environmental management system (certificate GB-E-30871, BSI, valid to 14 March 2027). Significant aspects are reviewed annually and include energy, waste, hazardous substances and transport. We report Scope 1 and 2 emissions annually and have a carbon reduction plan with a 2040 net-zero target, with a 23% reduction achieved against our 2019 baseline. Waste is segregated at both sites with 91% diverted from landfill in the last financial year.

answers.question: What insurance cover do you hold? Please state employers liability, public liability and professional indemnity limits.
answers.answer: We hold {{insurerEL}}, {{insurerPL}} and {{insurerPI}} cover with Aviva, renewing annually on 1 April. Certificates are available on request and copies are attached.

answers.question: Please confirm your compliance with the Modern Slavery Act 2015 and describe the steps you take in your supply chain.
answers.answer: We comply with the Modern Slavery Act 2015 and publish an annual statement approved by the board. Our Modern Slavery and Ethical Trading Policy (POL-11 v4) is applied to all suppliers through our supplier approval process, which requires suppliers to confirm compliance, and risk-based audits of higher-risk categories (labour agencies and overseas fabrication). All managers and buyers complete modern slavery awareness training; no instances have been identified.

answers.question: How do you protect personal data and information? Describe your information security arrangements and any certification.
answers.answer: We hold Cyber Essentials Plus certification (valid to 30 September 2027) and operate an information security policy set aligned to ISO 27001 controls, owned by {{dpo}} who acts as our data protection lead. Controls include multi-factor authentication on all systems, encrypted laptops and mobile devices, role-based access, nightly off-site backups tested quarterly, patch management within 14 days of release and annual staff training with phishing simulation. We are registered with the ICO and have had no reportable breaches.

answers.question: Describe your business continuity and disaster recovery arrangements.
answers.answer: Our Business Continuity Plan (POL-14 v3) covers loss of site, loss of IT, loss of key supplier and loss of key people, with recovery time objectives agreed for each critical activity. Both sites can support each other for fabrication capacity, IT systems are cloud-hosted with a 4-hour recovery objective and the plan is exercised annually; the last exercise (loss of IT scenario) was completed with all objectives met.

answers.question: What is your approach to equality, diversity and inclusion?
answers.answer: Our Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Policy (POL-07 v5) applies to recruitment, training, promotion and conduct. All staff complete EDI training at induction and every two years; managers complete additional unconscious-bias training. We monitor workforce data annually and report gender pay information. We are a Disability Confident Committed employer and an Armed Forces Covenant signatory.

answers.question: Do you have an anti-bribery and corruption policy? Please describe the controls in place.
answers.answer: Yes. Our Anti-Bribery and Corruption Policy (POL-09 v3) is based on the Bribery Act 2010 adequate-procedures guidance. Controls include a gifts and hospitality register with a £50 threshold, due diligence on agents and intermediaries, a whistleblowing line operated independently and annual training for all staff with authority to commit spend.

answers.question: How do you select, approve and monitor subcontractors and suppliers?
answers.answer: Suppliers and subcontractors are approved through our Supplier Management module in iMS OS. Approval requires evidence of insurance, relevant certification (ISO or SSIP), H&S performance, financial standing and policy acknowledgements, scored against clause 8.4 criteria. Critical suppliers are re-evaluated annually and certificates are chased automatically before expiry. Subcontractors working on site are inducted, supervised and included in our audit and inspection programme.

answers.question: Describe how you measure and report performance to customers (KPIs).
answers.answer: We agree KPIs at contract start, typically on-time delivery, right-first-time, safety performance and response times, and report monthly through a customer dashboard. Current group performance is 97.8% on-time delivery and 99.1% right-first-time. Non-conformances and complaints are managed through our corrective action process with root-cause analysis and customer sign-off.

answers.question: What social value will you deliver through this contract?
answers.answer: We deliver social value through local employment and apprenticeships (12 apprentices currently, 6% of workforce), a schools engineering outreach programme reaching around 600 pupils a year, volunteering days for all staff and local supply-chain spend (68% within 30 miles of our sites). Social value commitments are tracked against the TOMs framework and reported quarterly.

answers.question: Please describe your training and competence arrangements for staff carrying out the work.
answers.answer: Competence requirements are defined per role in our Training & Competency module in iMS OS, which gives a live training matrix with validity periods and renewal alerts. All operatives hold CSCS/CPCS as appropriate, lifting operations are supervised by an Appointed Person (LEEA/CPCS A61) and welders are coded to BS EN ISO 9606-1. Induction, toolbox talks and refresher training are recorded against each person, and competence is checked before equipment is issued.

services.name: Lifting equipment supply, installation and LOLER thorough examination
services.description: We design, manufacture, install and maintain overhead cranes, hoists, gantries and lifting accessories up to 50 tonnes SWL, and provide LOLER 1998 thorough examinations through our in-house competent persons (LEEA registered). Work is planned under our ISO 9001 and ISO 45001 management system with a named project manager, a lift plan for every installation and a handover pack with test certificates and O&M information.
services.method: Our method follows five stages: survey and lift plan; design and manufacture to BS EN 15011 / BS EN 13001; delivery and installation under permit to work with exclusion zones; load testing and commissioning witnessed by the client; and handover with LOLER certificates, O&M manuals and a scheduled examination programme in iMS OS so renewals are never missed.
people: M. Grant (Operations Director, 24 years lifting equipment)
D. Brooks (H&S Advisor, NEBOSH, Appointed Person A61)

services.name: Structural steelwork fabrication and erection
services.description: We fabricate structural steelwork to EN 1090-2 EXC3 (CE/UKCA marked) at Northfield Works and erect on site with our own crews, including access platforms, walkways, pipe bridges and plant support structures for utilities, process and rail clients.
services.method: Fabrication drawings are produced in Tekla and checked by our chartered engineer; welding is to BS EN ISO 3834-2 by coded welders; site erection uses RAMS reviewed by the client, with crane lifts planned by an Appointed Person. Inspection and test plans are agreed before start and signed off at each hold point.

services.name: Mechanical services maintenance for water and utilities sites
services.description: We provide planned and reactive mechanical maintenance for pumps, screens, penstocks, cranes and lifting equipment on water treatment and utilities sites, with a 4-hour emergency response within 60 miles of our depots and 24/7 call-out.
services.method: Planned maintenance is scheduled in iMS OS against each asset with QR-coded asset tags; engineers follow task-specific RAMS, record findings on site and raise follow-up actions automatically. Reactive work is triaged by our 24/7 desk with a 4-hour response for critical assets. Monthly performance reports cover response times, first-time fix and compliance with LOLER/PUWER inspections.
people: R. Osei (Lead Engineer, water sector 11 years)

questions.answer:
Every contract is mobilised through a 4-week plan led by a named contract manager: site inductions, asset data capture, RAMS approval, KPI baseline and a client kick-off, with weekly reporting through a shared dashboard.

Week 1: contract manager appointed, kick-off, site access and inductions, insurances and RAMS issued. Week 2: asset survey and QR tagging, schedules loaded into iMS OS. Week 3: trial planned visits, KPI baseline agreed. Week 4: full service live, first weekly report. Key personnel are named in the bid and may not be changed without client agreement.

This work is led by M. Grant (Operations Director).

Mobilisation and contract management

questions.text: How do you select, approve and monitor subcontractors and suppliers?
questions.answer: Suppliers and subcontractors are approved through our Supplier Management module in iMS OS. Approval requires evidence of insurance, relevant certification (ISO or SSIP), H&S performance, financial standing and policy acknowledgements, scored against clause 8.4 criteria. Critical suppliers are re-evaluated annually and certificates are chased automatically before expiry. Subcontractors working on site are inducted, supervised and included in our audit and inspection programme.

questions.text: Describe your business continuity and disaster recovery arrangements.
questions.answer: Our Business Continuity Plan (POL-14 v3) covers loss of site, loss of IT, loss of key supplier and loss of key people, with recovery time objectives agreed for each critical activity. Both sites can support each other for fabrication capacity, IT systems are cloud-hosted with a 4-hour recovery objective and the plan is exercised annually; the last exercise (loss of IT scenario) was completed with all objectives met.
